title: Lifting an initial computation
statement: Let $M$ and $B$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines, with $M$ using no more work tapes than $B$. Let $e$ map the states of $M$ to states of $B$, and suppose that at every embedded state and for every input/work-tape scan, $B$ takes the padded action of $M$, reading the corresponding initial work-tape block. If $M$ computes output $y$ from input $x$ in time $T$, then $B$, started in state $e(q_0)$ with all work tapes blank on input $x$, is halted at time $T$ and has output $y$.
hypotheses_covered: For all source states, input symbols, and host work-symbol assignments, the host transition is the padded source transition read from its first $M.k$ tapes
replaced:
Suppose a host machine simulates a source machine by padded transitions on an
initial tape block. If the source computes $y$ from input $x$ within $T$ steps,
then the host, started in the embedded initial state at the empty seam on $x$,
is halted at time $T$ with output $y$; this holds even for a source with no work
tapes.
